$comment: Canonical UI screen registry — the AI's map of the app's screens. Each screen maps to its route, the module it belongs to (module_key), a one-line purpose, and the AI action_keys reachable from it. Keep this in sync when adding a route (see doc/AI_READINESS.md). Ingested into the AI global corpus by src/services/ai/knowledge/codebase.js; also usable by the frontend for nav/breadcrumbs.
$comment_actions: `actions[]` is now COMPLETE for every <module>.ai.js manifest action, not just a sample. It is read in both directions: screen->actions grounds the assistant ('where do I raise an invoice?'), and the INVERSION action->route is how src/services/ai/answer-sources.js turns the reads the orchestrator executed into the citations under an answer. An action missing here is an answer that cannot say where it read from, so tests/unit/ai-readiness.test.js asserts every manifest read is declared on exactly one screen. Where a module owns several screens the split is by entity, not by module_key (MOD-64's signatures live on /vault/signatures, its documents on /vault/documents).
$comment_search: Search that finds everything (meeting 6, PR 4 — G5). ⌘K reads this file for pages: every screen carries title_fr (and optional synonyms beside the shared list in packages/shared/schemas/search.js); hubs[] are the area landing pages (kept out of screens[] on purpose — route-access and the ribbon read screens[], and a hub is gated by its sections); redirects[] are old addresses that still work; section_hubs[] are hubs that keep their sections in their own component; tabs[] are every URL-addressable 360 tab (useUrlTab), with the record types they open on. app: public-web marks a screen served by the public site rather than this app. scripts/check-search-registry.js fails the build on a route, hub section, tab or record module this file does not account for, and on an entry the code no longer has.

screens.purpose: The tenant's public articles: headline, address, tags and publish state, with creation reduced to a headline. Publishing is its own action and is refused until the article has an address and a body. One explicit save with a discard warning, because an article is one long text rather than a set of independent blocks. The cover uploads through the vault and saves immediately, since an upload that waited for Save would leave an orphaned public document.

screens.title: Lead 360
screens.purpose: Full dossier for a single lead — Overview, Meetings (with the F1 discovery sections and their capture state), Quote requests, Proposals, Opportunities, Enquiries triaged in, and the audit history. The join F6 made necessary: the funnel, the intake lifecycle and the pipeline stage live on three different rows, so this is the one place that shows a company's whole story. Money is gated on finance visibility. Its reads are declared on the registers above; this screen adds no manifest action of its own.

screens.title: Contact Enquiries

Replying sends the email through the tenant's SUPPORT identity and only marks the enquiry RESPONDED if it lands; every attempt, including failures, is kept. Triage raises a lead and/or a partnership request without touching the correspondence status.

screens.title: Quote Requests

screens.title: Intake 360

'Is it converted' is read from converted_opportunity_id, never from the status value. Its reads are declared on the register above; this screen adds no manifest action of its own.

An audience switch appears only for callers whose grants let them see beyond their own work.

screens.title: Calendar
screens.purpose: The month grid with the month's agenda beneath it. Booking two events in the same place at the same time warns with the conflicting rows and lets the user book anyway, rather than refusing.

screens.title: Analytics
screens.purpose: Operational analysis of the SAME authorised task population Tasks and Today show: open work and its composition, overdue aging, throughput, cycle time, workload by assignee, blocked work and the backlog burn-down. Every figure reconciles with the Tasks list because it is produced by the same visibility predicate, every chart has a table beside it, and every drill-down opens the list filtered the same way. Deliberately operational — it carries no appraisal score, compensation input or employee KPI rating, which remain in Empower HR under their own permissions.

Distinct from AI Control, which governs the assistant rather than using it.
